newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia says mass privatisation list due soon.
newsitem.headline: Croatia says mass privatisation list due soon.

text.p: A list of Croatian companies to be included in the mass privatisation scheme is being finalised and could be published very soon, Privatisation minister said on Friday.

"We do have problems in determining how many (government) shares to include but they will be among the best available in the remaining portfolio of the Privatisation Fund," Damir Ostovic told Reuters during an annual Zagreb bourse conference.

He said the list could include up to as many as 600 firms, with some of the country's leading tourist and shipping and industrial enterprises among them, because government holdings in some of them were very small.
Ostovic would not venture any names.
The mass voucher scheme was originaly planned to involve between 200 and 300 companies which have been partly privatised in employee buyouts or through other schemes.

But Ostovic said many of them in which the state privatisation agency still has a stake, were in the process of denominating their share capital, usualy from German marks they had been expressed in into kuna.
The agency is also in the process of swapping some of its holdings with two pension funds and some banks to increase stakes in a smaller number of firms and ease portfolio management.
A critical mass of assets to be offered for voucher privatisation would be 2.5 billion marks or more, depending on the number of beneficiaries, Ostovic said.

"In about two weeks when we know exactly how much can be offered and in what firms, the registration of beneficiaries can begin," he said adding that their number could be anywhere between 200,000-400,000.
Those eleigible for the distribution of vouchers, to be swapped for shares in companies sometime next year, will be war victims and all other citizens who did not take part in employee buyouts.
The pace of the whole scheme could depend on available budget funds required, which are estimated at 25 million kuna, Ostovic said. --Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
